evidence: The schema now permits only six non-consequential actions: two suggestion actions, two reversible-preparation actions, and two approved reversible-execution actions. Intent acceptance, scope mutation, and direct external-egress authority are not members of the vocabulary.

Equivalent generated validators order human-only, suggest, prepare-reversible, and execute-reversible levels and reject any allowed action above the selected level while continuing to require false mayAcceptIntent/mayChangeScope plus intent-acceptance and scope-change human gates.

Every declared stopping condition must belong to the selected mode's closed set, and at least one mode-required condition must be present; resource-budget is allowed only as a secondary cross-mode condition. Non-local egress requires both an opaque approved destination and the external-egress human gate, while local-only permits neither.

Fourteen TypeScript and twelve Python research-intent tests pass with equivalent denials for accept-intent, change-scope, external-egress, action/level escalation, systematic-plus-technical stopping, non-local egress without a gate, and local-only egress with a contradictory gate.

Valid boundaries cover empty human-only actions, suggestion-only actions, prepare-reversible actions, execute-approved actions at execute-reversible, all seven lawful mode stopping sets with resource-budget, and approved-redacted egress with one destination plus the external-egress human gate.

All 55 TypeScript contracts, 51 Python contracts, 38 service tests, and six packaging tests pass, preserving the original revision, governing-reference, lineage, draft, ownership, and sidecar behavior.

The semantic-rule catalog, closed schema vocabulary, deterministic generator, TypeScript/Python templates and outputs, parity tests, package documentation, architecture contract, and accepted ADR-0023 are synchronized; generation, strict compilation, quality, architecture, ADR, and build provenance pass.

No migration, persistence, UI, service enforcement, provider, network, credential, dependency, or external-system behavior changed. Runtime enforcement and durable audit remain later approved task duties.
The original R01 evidence and finding ledger remain append-only and are included in the exact strict-descendant changed-path boundary.

reviewerDisposition.rootCauseAnalysis: The initial schema bounded action spelling but not authority meaning, while generated semantic checks treated the mayAcceptIntent/mayChangeScope flags, required gates, egress destinations, and stopping conditions as independent fields. The stopping validator used any-match intersection, so one lawful condition masked an incompatible condition. R02 closes those relationships with one canonical action vocabulary and level rank, one egress destination/gate invariant, and one required-plus-subset stopping rule, implemented identically in generated TypeScript and Python and covered by parity tests.
